lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fábia | Lesson 5 -- What We Must, What We Can

listenings.text: Fabia, this is the list from head office, so let me be precise about what is negotiable and what is not. Two things are non-negotiable. There must be a full audit trail on every change, and in the event of a breach we must be notified within twenty-four hours, in writing. Those two are not preferences, they are conditions of the group policy. Then there is one thing we recommend rather than require: there should be a quarterly call between your team and ours, so nobody discovers a problem in an email. And a warning on timing. Legal still has to review the contract, and that may take another two weeks. So please do not plan around signing this month.

So, they asked me who has access to the data, and I said, well, only a few people, usually. Then they asked what happens if there is a leak, and I said we would try to let them know as quickly as we could. And when they asked about their auditors, I said we could probably arrange something. I thought I was being honest. Looking back, every answer I gave sounded like a maybe. They asked for the same answers in writing, and after that they simply stopped replying. I lost that account on the words, not on the price.

matching.title: Match the word to its meaning
defs: the record of who changed what, and when
legal responsibility if something goes wrong
the duty not to share what you know

items.situation: "Who can see our payroll data?" Answer with the number and the obligation.
"What happens if there is a breach?" This one is regulatory, not policy. Say so.
tips: That is not our policy, it is regulatory.

items.situation: You want their data by the tenth. Ask head office politely, but do not sound optional.
tips: Could you send us ... by the tenth?
We would need it by ... to be safe.

items.situation: They ask for something you are able to do but are not obliged to. Say yes clearly.
tips: That is not required, but we can.

items.situation: You are not certain the timeline holds at 400 employees. Say it honestly, without alarming them.
tips: Onboarding may take an extra week at that volume.
I'd rather tell you now than in month two.

arguebank.label: Useful language
items: B sounds ... , and on compliance that reads as risk.
A client wants to hear must, not we try to.
If I were the client, I would ...
That answer leaves too much open.
You can be firm and still be polite.
